title: Platform Ops Inference Adoption Playbook 2026
author: Priya Nair
body:
Overview

This playbook equips sellers and solutions engineers to engage Platform and Infrastructure (Platform Ops) buyers who own inference deployment decisions. It bundles positioning, a compact competitive brief, pricing scenarios, pilot-architectures, risk-reduction tactics, and a security FAQ tailored for technical procurement conversations. Use this document during discovery, pilot scoping, and commercial proposals.

Audience and intent

- Primary personas: Platform Engineering Lead, ML Platform Engineer, Infrastructure Architect, Head of Cloud/Platform.
- Secondary personas: Security/Compliance, Procurement, Applied ML.
- Intent: shorten evaluation cycles by translating platform-level concerns (latency, isolation, cost predictability, operational tooling) into concrete pilot designs and negotiable commercial terms.

Elevator pitch (two-line and technical follow-up)

- Two-line: Redwood Inference provides a unified inference runtime that delivers predictable latency, transparent unit economics, and consistent operational tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments—so platform teams can standardize model serving without building the stack.
- Technical follow-up: We combine a GPU-optimized serving runtime (continuous batching, KV caching, quantization profiles) with a control plane that supports pinning model versions, canary rollouts, and routing policies (region/latency/cost). This enables identical APIs and observability across hosted, dedicated, and VPC deployments.

Key platform-level differentiators to emphasize

1) Unified operational model across environments
- Same API, SDK, and rollout primitives for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; reduces onboarding and runbook drift.

2) Predictable unit economics and clear knobs
- Exposed levers (batching, cache TTL, quantization profile) with tooling that simulates cost impact and recommends configurations by workload.

3) Production-first reliability and graceful degradation
- Automated fallback policies: model variants, region failover, and tiered capacity to keep critical routes live under stress.

4) Observability built for platform controls
- Token-level cost breakdown, per-model latency distributions, tracing hooks into customer services, per-route dashboards and anomaly alerts.

Competitive brief (concise)

- Hyperscaler endpoint services (AWS SageMaker Endpoints, GCP Vertex AI): strong for integrated cloud workflows and existing procurement relationships. Weakness: less turnkey batching/kv caching for LLMs and fewer rollout primitives tuned for multimodel fallbacks.
- LLM API providers (single-API providers): very easy to start; downside is limited deployment models (usually hosted-only) and less transparency on per-token economics and private deployment options.
- Inference runtime vendors / open-source stacks (custom Triton/LLM or in-house runtimes): deep control and low marginal cost at scale; downside: long build time, hidden maintenance costs, missing standardized rollouts and enterprise support.

Competitive positioning map (talk track)

- If buyer asks about total cost vs hyperscaler: highlight the predictability gains from reserved capacity and the ability to optimize quantization/batching to shave per-token costs. Offer a cost modeling session.
- If they plan to self-host: stress time-to-production, operational support, and the economics of engineering effort vs managed dedicated/private options.

Pilot architectures and recommended scoping patterns

We recommend three canonical pilot models. For each, include success criteria and a 6–8 week activation checklist.

1) Hosted-to-Dedicated Ramp (recommended for SaaS platform teams)
- Scope: Start with Redwood hosted API for prod-like traffic on a narrow set of routes (search reranking, chat assistant). After validating quality and latency, reserve Dedicated capacity and migrate traffic gradually.
- Success criteria (example): median generation latency < 250ms, 99th percentile < 1.2s, cost per 1k tokens matches modeled target within +/- 15%, no regression on 90% of automated QA prompts.
- Activation checklist (6–8 weeks):
  1. Discovery: define routes, expected QPS, SLO targets, data residency needs.
  2. Test harness: upload eval prompt sets and baseline model; run A/B with traffic shadowing.
  3. Observe & tune: gather latency, token-cost, and quality metrics; apply batching/quantization recommendations.
  4. Commit: reserve Dedicated pool with burst policy; perform canary migration (1%, 10%, 50%, 100%).

2) Private VPC Pilot (recommended for regulated customers or strict egress controls)
- Scope: Deploy Redwood Private control plane with customer-managed VPC connectors to the customer’s compute or the dedicated hardware in customer tenancy.
- Success criteria: validated network egress rules, KMS integration for key management, audit log export, and sample application integration for full CI pipelines.
- Activation checklist: network and IAM design, KMS/HSM proofing, compliance policy mapping, runbook handover.

3) Edge Hybrid Pilot (recommended for latency-critical regional workloads)
- Scope: Co-located inference nodes (on-prem or edge cloud) with central Redwood control plane. Use caching and region-aware routing to keep hot contexts local.
- Success criteria: p99 latency within target region SLO, consistent model versioning across edge nodes, offline fallback behavior tested.

Pricing guidance and sample scenarios

- Pricing primitives we can negotiate: hosted per-token tiers, dedicated capacity commit (monthly/annual), pilot discounts, ingress/egress network allowances, support/uptime tier.

- Sample pricing scenarios (illustrative only)

| Scenario | Traffic | Suggested Product | Commercial levers | Monthly ballpark cost |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| Early pilot | 10 QPS, 60k tokens/day | Hosted API with pilot credits | Pilot discount (50%), limited SLAs | $2k–$6k |
| Platform POC -> Dedicated | 100 QPS, 600k tokens/day | Dedicated small pool (reserved) + burst | 6–12 month commit, usage cap | $18k–$40k |
| Large production | 500 QPS, 3M tokens/day | Dedicated fleet + optional private VPC | Multi-year commit, volume discount | $80k–$220k |

Note: provide a dedicated cost-modeling session that uses the customer’s token mix, average prompt/response lengths, and peak concurrency to produce precise figures. Always qualify pilot discounts and credits in an SOW with clear handoff criteria.

Commercial playbook: pilot to procurement handoff

1) Pilot SOW: define routes, success criteria, timeline, owners, and termination criteria. Include a clause that maps pilot metrics to commercial commitments (e.g., if SLOs met, apply pilot usage to first month of committed capacity).
2) Runbook & Handover: deliver runbooks (canary, rollback, incident playbook) and a joint runbook review meeting before procurement kickoff.
3) Procurement packs: template contract language for Dedicated and Private (SLA language, data residency clause, termination/fallback options).

Risk and objection handling (common platform objections)

- "We already have cloud vendor credits / prefer single-vendor consolidation."
  Response: acknowledge integration benefits; call out specialized inference optimizations (continuous batching, KV caching, quantization) that can materially reduce per-token cost and engineering time. Offer a side-by-side latency and cost simulation.
- "We want to own everything in-house."
  Response: present TCO comparison including engineering hours for building, hardening, and sustaining a production inference stack; propose a hybrid approach to retain control over sensitive workloads while outsourcing operational surface area.
- "How do we avoid vendor lock-in?"
  Response: explain model/version pinning, exportable configuration manifests, documented migration path, and vendor-agnostic SDK patterns we encourage.

Security & compliance FAQ (for Platform/Infra conversations)

Q: How are customer models and data isolated in Dedicated and Private?
A: Dedicated capacity is tenant-isolated at the GPU pool level and namespaces; Private provides a customer-managed control plane with VPC connectors. Both options support KMS/HSM integrations for key lifecycle management and strict egress controls.

Q: Can we bring our own KMS or integrate with HSM?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS integrations and HSM-backed key stores for signing models and encrypting KV caches. Provide your security contact for a technical onboarding checklist.

Q: Where do logs and audit trails live?
A: Audit logs are exportable to the customer’s SIEM (syslog/Kinesis/Cloud PubSub). We retain service logs in encrypted partitions; audit retention can be configured per contract.

Q: Are there SOC/ISO certifications and penetration testing evidence available?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 readiness; we provide redacted penetration test reports under NDA and can supply compliance artifacts (gap analysis) during procurement.

Q: How do you manage model provenance and supply-chain risk?
A: We maintain a model catalog with provenance metadata (model version, source, hash), cryptographic signing for verified model builds, and a model-onboarding approval workflow for enterprise customers.

Pilot activation checklist (operational)

- Who: Sales AE (owner), SE (technical lead), Customer Platform Eng (customer lead), Security Eng (customer).
- Pre-activation artifacts: signed pilot SOW, network diagram, credential exchange sheet, evaluation prompt set, target SLOs.
- Week-by-week plan:
  Week 0: Kickoff, discovery, and environment access.
  Week 1: Baseline tests, sample integration, and observability tags.
  Week 2–3: Load testing, tuning batching/quantization, A/B evaluation.
  Week 4–6: Canary rollout (if migrating production), runbook handover, procurement briefing.

Sales-ready collateral (quick list)

- One-pager: "Why platform teams choose Redwood" (technical bullets + 3 ROI scenarios).
- Architecture diagrams: hosted→dedicated migration flow, Private VPC layout, edge hybrid.
- Cost modeling workbook: Excel/Sheets template with fields for prompts, token sizes, concurrency.
- Compliance packet: SOC2 summary, audit log integration steps, KMS/HSM checklist.

Appendix: Example SLA and SLO targets to propose

- Availability SLA (for Dedicated): 99.9% monthly uptime with defined maintenance windows.
- Latency SLOs (per-route): median < 250ms, p95 < 800ms, p99 < 1.5s (adjust per model class and sequence length).
- Error budget: 1% monthly request failure budget for non-degraded responses; automated rollback triggers when exceeded.

Ownership and next steps

- AE playbook: schedule cost-model session within 5 business days of discovery call.
- SE playbook: deliver pilot runbook and metrics dashboard 48 hours after baseline run.
- Procurement pack: attach template SOW and compliance packet when moving to procurement.
